evals.name: new-system-conceptual-logical
evals.prompt: Here's the requirements map for our class booking system (evals/files/booking-requirements-map.md). Design the architecture: conceptual and logical, no detailed spec yet. Write it to docs/design/booking-design.md.
evals.expected_output: A conceptual + logical design doc traced to the map's IDs, with a coverage table that closes.
expectations: The doc states its depth (conceptual + logical) and why near the top
Q-1 (late-cancel fee scope) is handled as a blocking question or a stated working assumption
The context map marks at least one trust boundary and names threats at it
Components are named after the domain, not technology products
The logical level names no products other than those forced by a CON-n (Stripe, PostgreSQL)
A data ownership table gives each datum exactly one owner
Scenario walkthroughs name the contract at each hop and together cover FR-1 to FR-4
NFR-1 has a mechanism with a line of arithmetic or capacity reasoning
NFR-3 (never overbooked) has a concrete mechanism, such as a transactional or conditional update
A coverage table lists every FR and NFR with a component, and every component lists requirement IDs

evals.name: small-change-stays-conceptual
evals.prompt: In our existing booking system (see evals/files/booking-requirements-map.md), we just want to add FR-5, the waitlist. The rest of the architecture is settled. Give me the design for that.
evals.expected_output: A short design that picks conceptual-only (or a compressed logical pass) and says what it compressed and why.
expectations: The doc states a reduced depth and the reason (a change inside a settled architecture)
It says which sections it compressed or skipped instead of padding every template heading
The waitlist design cites FR-5 and addresses how it interacts with NFR-3 (no overbooking)
The answer is clearly shorter than a full conceptual + logical doc

evals.name: detailed-spec-for-implementers
evals.prompt: We're handing the booking system (evals/files/booking-requirements-map.md) to a contractor team who weren't in any of our discussions. Write the full design, all the way to an implementation-ready spec for the booking component.
evals.expected_output: A doc at all three levels, with the booking component specified to mock-ready detail and every acceptance criterion mapped to a test.
expectations: The doc states its depth as all three levels because the readers are outside implementers
The booking interface has at least one literal request and response example
Error cases for booking are enumerated (for example class full, already booked)
The physical data model justifies at least one index by a query or NFR
Failure modes for Stripe cover timeout, retry with idempotency, and Stripe being down
A test strategy table maps each acceptance criterion of FR-1 to FR-4 to a named test with a type
NFR-1 gets a load test and a latency budget split across hops
Products are pinned only at the detailed level, each pivotal one with alternatives
